about: The Mac's own worksheet R examples, in the schema of the shared Learn/Upstream/WorksheetR/examples.json, for what only the Mac's grid and loader can show: number cells that keep their typed text, formula cells refused once the workbook has been edited (RULES.md section 7), the 1904 date system (rule 3.9: each loader's date system is tested separately), answers agreed with Windows on 21 November 2026, after learning-v1.1.7 (date-times anchor the any-case missing words, Excel's built-in formats 45 and 47 are times of day, and whole columns that are every column of the grid are the entire worksheet) and after learning-v1.1.9 (a time of day is judged on its value before it is rounded, a date after; a duration of more days than the last day's serial, of either sign, is a number; every rounding to the millisecond is half away from zero), text the loader reads from Excel's _xHHHH_ escapes, and a list of vectors, which the Mac's 8 MiB script limits by its values alone, never by its area. Tests/test_worksheet_r_examples.py runs these with the shared cases.

schema.extends: the schema of Learn/Upstream/WorksheetR/examples.json, with the three additions below
schema.typed: a cell {"typed": "<text>"} is not in the file: it is typed into the grid once the workbook is open, through the grid's own edit path (store.apply, then workbook.changed(), as onCellsEdited does). A number typed so keeps its text (" 13", "1.50"), and the workbook then counts as edited, so its formula results may be out of date
schema.dateSystem: 1904: the workbook uses the 1904 date system (workbookPr date1904), and the case's serials are serials of that system
schema.refusedNaming: left out when the refusal names no cell

cases.name: Number cells keep their typed text and count as their numbers

expect.r: structure(list(c(13, 1.5, 5), c("1.5", "x", "13")), names = c("n", "c"), row.names = c(NA_integer_, -3L), class = "data.frame")

cases.note: The Mac grid stores typed " 13", "1.50" and "5." as number cells that keep the text typed, where Excel would hold 13, 1.5 and 5. Rule 3.4 reads each as its number; in a character column a number cell is its rule 3.7 text, String(x).

cases.name: A typed number used as a heading is its number's text

expect.r: structure(list(c(1), c(2)), names = c("2.5", "b"), row.names = c(NA_integer_, -1L), class = "data.frame")

cases.name: An edited workbook refuses formula cells

expect.refusedMessage: Recalculate and save this workbook in Excel, then reopen it before using formula cells in R.

cases.note: C1, outside the selection, is typed once the workbook is open. The Mac cannot recalculate, so after any edit, in any cell of any sheet, a formula's saved result may be out of date.

cases.name: An unedited workbook sends a formula's saved result

expect.r: structure(list(c(2, 4)), names = c("Dose"), row.names = c(NA_integer_, -2L), class = "data.frame")

cases.name: The 1904 date system: dates from 1904-01-01, times of day and date-times

comments: # Dates without a time of day are R Date values; other dates and times are text.
expect.r: structure(list(structure(c(-24107, -24047), class = "Date"), c("14:30:00", "06:00:00"), c("1904-01-01 12:00:00", "1904-03-01 18:00:00")), names = c("Date", "Time", "When"), row.names = c(NA_integer_, -2L), class = "data.frame")

cases.note: In the 1904 system serial 0 is 1904-01-01, and serial 60 is 1904-03-01, an ordinary day.

cases.name: Date-times anchor the any-case missing words; times of day do not

comments: # Dates without a time of day are R Date values; other dates and times are text.
expect.r: structure(list(c("2026-11-21 10:00:00", NA), c("14:30:00", "na")), names = c("When", "At"), row.names = c(NA_integer_, -2L), class = "data.frame")

cases.note: Agreed with Windows on 21 November 2026, after learning-v1.1.7: date-times, as well as numbers, Booleans and dates, anchor the any-case words of rule 3.2. A time of day does not.

cases.name: Excel's built-in formats 45 (mm:ss) and 47 (mmss.0) are times of day; only [h], [m] and [s] make a duration

comments: # Dates without a time of day are R Date values; other dates and times are text.

cases.note: Agreed with Windows on 21 November 2026, after learning-v1.1.7. Built-ins 45 and 47 wrap at the hour, so a value below one day is a time of day; from one day it is a date-time, and below zero a number, as for any time-of-day format. Built-in 46, [h]:mm:ss, is a duration: 26:00:00 and -01:00:00.

cases.name: Text Excel stores with _xHHHH_ escapes arrives exactly

expect.r: structure(list(c("a\r\nb", "x\u0001y\u001f", "\ufffe\uffff", "_x0041_ and _x005F_")), names = c("A"), row.names = c(NA_integer_, -4L), class = "data.frame")

cases.note: The file holds CR, C0 controls and U+FFFE and U+FFFF as Excel writes them, _x000D_, _x0001_ and so on, and the text _x0041_ as _x005F_x0041_; the Mac's loader reads each back as the character.

cases.name: Whole columns that are every column of the grid are the entire worksheet

expect.r: structure(list(c(1, NA), c(NA, 2)), names = c("a", "b"), row.names = c(NA_integer_, -2L), class = "data.frame")

cases.note: Amendment 1 to rule 2.6, agreed with Windows on 21 November 2026. The Mac grid opens this file with columns A to C, so A, B and C, however they were selected (one drag, Shift-click, or Command-click pieces, which Glide's CompactSelection hands over as one list), are every column of the sheet: Entire worksheet, B2:C4. As ordinary whole columns (rule 2.3) they would be A2:C4, with A kept as NA.

cases.name: A time format below one day is a time of day, judged on its value and then rounded, so 0.999999999 is 24:00:00; a date is judged after rounding

comments: # Dates without a time of day are R Date values; other dates and times are text.
expect.r: structure(list(c("24:00:00"), structure(c(-25567), class = "Date")), names = c("Clock", "When"), row.names = c(NA_integer_, -1L), class = "data.frame")

cases.note: Agreed with Windows on 21 November 2026, after learning-v1.1.9. 0.999999999 is below one day, so in h:mm:ss it is a time of day, whatever it rounds to; rounded to the millisecond it is a whole day, written 24:00:00. A date or date-time is judged after rounding: 0.9999999999 in yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss rounds to serial 1, the date 1900-01-01.

cases.name: In the 1904 date system, 0.999999999 in a time format is 24:00:00 too, and a duration beyond its last day is a number

comments: # Dates without a time of day are R Date values; other dates and times are text.
expect.r: structure(list(c("24:00:00"), structure(c(-24106), class = "Date"), c(2957003.25), c("70968072:00:00")), names = c("Clock", "When", "Over", "Last"), row.names = c(NA_integer_, -1L), class = "data.frame")

cases.note: Agreed with Windows on 21 November 2026, after learning-v1.1.9. In the 1904 system 0.9999999999 in yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss rounds to serial 1, 1904-01-02, and the last day, 9999-12-31, is serial 2,957,003: a duration of 2,957,003.25 days is beyond it, so a number, and one of 2,957,003 days is 70968072:00:00.

cases.name: A duration beyond the last day as a number of days, of either sign, is a number

comments: # Dates without a time of day are R Date values; other dates and times are text.
expect.r: structure(list(c(2958465.25), c(-3000000), c("71003160:00:00"), c("-71003160:00:00")), names = c("Over", "Negative", "Longest", "Most negative"), row.names = c(NA_integer_, -1L), class = "data.frame")

cases.note: Agreed with Windows on 21 November 2026, after learning-v1.1.9: a duration is a number when its absolute value is beyond the last day of the date system, 2,958,465 in the 1900 system, judged on the value itself. So 2958465.25 and -3000000 are numbers, while 2958465 and -2958465 days are durations.

cases.name: Rounding to the millisecond is half away from zero: half a millisecond is 00:00:00.001

comments: # Dates without a time of day are R Date values; other dates and times are text.
expect.r: structure(list(c("00:00:00.001"), c("-00:00:00.001"), c("00:00:00.001"), c("00:00:00.003")), names = c("Duration", "Negative", "Clock", "Two and a half"), row.names = c(NA_integer_, -1L), class = "data.frame")

cases.note: Agreed with Windows on 21 November 2026, after learning-v1.1.9. 5.787037037037037e-09 days is exactly half a millisecond in IEEE doubles (times 86,400,000 it is 0.5), and 2.8935185185185185e-08 days two and a half. Rounding half to even would give 00:00:00 for the first three and 00:00:00.002 for the last.

cases.name: A list of vectors is not refused for its area when its values fit: two values in 9,437,184 cells

comments: # Missing values are removed separately from each vector.
expect.r: structure(list(c(1), logical(0), logical(0), logical(0), logical(0), logical(0), logical(0), logical(0), c(2)), names = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H", "I"))

cases.note: Codex's review of the Mac candidate, 21 November 2026: the Mac writes the values into the script, at most 8 MiB (RULES.md section 7), and a list holds only its non-missing values (rule 5.3), so only they count. Here the grid sends the two values alone, read from the two cells that hold them; the 9,437,184 cells of the area, more than one for each byte of the limit, cost nothing. As a data frame the same area is refused, since each of its cells needs at least NA.
